items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: he was one of my dear friends after we were on Kenton’s band together... finally get to work with my old pal.

ctx.x: Yeah. Coleman Hawkins I think was the first one, or Lester Young I guess. Lester and Hawk about the same time, because I mentioned all those Basie records that I heard and I knew that that guy was good. Then let’s see, Dexter Gordon, after I got out of the service I heard a lot of Dexter and then Al Cohn and Zoot Sims and Sonny Rollins and Coltrane I loved. I can’t say he was much of an influence outside of just making me just feel good, because the way he played was not my thing naturally, but I sure appreciated…
Yeah. He always made me feel a little on edge actually.
